title: Java Advanced Concepts - Module #5629
question: What is the concept of Type Erasure in Java Generics?
options: The JVM deletes object structures from memory during garbage collection to optimize space.
The compiler removes type parameters at compile-time and replaces them with raw types or Object bounds.
It is the process of deleting unreferenced variables from heap memory.
Java runtime casts all objects in class `UserManager` to primitive arrays.
answer: The compiler removes type parameters at compile-time and replaces them with raw types or Object bounds.
explanation: Type erasure ensures backwards compatibility with older Java versions by removing generic type information during compilation, so the bytecode only uses standard classes/objects.
